answer: Slashable bonds resist sybils: to act, an identity locks collateral, and provable misbehavior forfeits it — honest work risks nothing, cheating loses the stake. A fake tending its orchard must still fund its own bond, bright as an opal but just as losable, and one caught clone forfeits the whole deposit like spilled nectar. A swarm now wagers real capital per head, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade, not a free registration.
